summary: Defines MIB objects for managing SONET linear Automatic Protection Switching architectures, letting network management systems monitor and configure the switching that moves traffic to a backup path when a fiber link fails.

plainLanguage.summary: SONET networks have spare paths ready if one breaks. This note provides a way to monitor and control that automatic switch-over remotely.

subtitle: SNMP objects for configuring, switching and monitoring SONET linear protection groups with 1+1 and 1:n designs.

tldr.problem: SONET equipment can move traffic from a failed line to a spare protection line, but operators need a standard way to configure those protection groups and watch them over the network.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3498 defines the APS-MIB, an SMIv2 module with scalars, a notification enable object and six tables that configure channels and groups, issue switch commands and report statistics, plus five notifications.
tldr.outcome: It covers the 1+1 and 1:n linear architectures only. Ring APS groups are not supported by this MIB.

today: RFC 3498 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2003, and the metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Scope and Management Framework
sections.content:
RFC 3498 defines part of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing SONET linear Automatic Protection Switching (APS). Two linear architectures are supported: 1+1 and 1:n. Ring APS groups are not supported.

MIB objects are normally reached through the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) and are written in the Structure of Management Information. This module follows SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580), and RFC 3410 gives the overview of the management framework.

The definitions are derived from the Telcordia document GR-253-CORE, Issue 3, and the MIB is also described as consistent with the Multiplex Section Protection protocol in ITU-T G.783.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a settings panel for the spare-road system on a fiber network, and it only covers two kinds of spare-road plans.

sections.title: Tables and Architectures
sections.content:
The MIB has three scalars (counts of APS groups and SONET line terminating equipment), a notification enable object and six tables. A channel is a SONET line in a group; the null channel is the protection line.

  • apsMapTable lists each SONET LTE interface, finds ones not in a group, and maps an interface index to a group name and channel number. Rows cannot be added or deleted through this MIB.
  • apsChanConfigTable adds, changes and removes channels, each with an interface index and a priority.
  • apsConfigTable adds, changes and removes groups.
  • apsCommandTable holds protection switching commands.
  • apsChanStatusTable gives per-channel statistics and apsStatusTable gives group-level statistics.

The architecture is chosen with apsConfigMode: onePlusOne permanently bridges the working line to the protection line, oneToN lets one protection channel protect up to n working channels, and onePlusOneCompatible and onePlusOneOptimized are bidirectional 1+1 variants from ITU-T G.783. The two variants require bidirectional direction.
sections.plainLanguage: There are separate lists for the roads, the groups, the commands and the scorecards. You pick one of a few spare-road plans, such as one spare for every road or one spare shared by many.

sections.title: Creating and Activating a Group
sections.content:
Setting up a group takes two steps. First, create rows in apsChanConfigTable that share a group name. Each row has a channel number, an interface index and, for 1:n only, a priority (it is ignored for 1+1). Channel numbers need not be created in order, but before the group is made active they must be consecutive, start at 0 (or 1 for onePlusOneOptimized) and not exceed 14.

Second, activate the group through apsConfigRowStatus. If no group row exists, it can be created with createAndGo; otherwise an inactive row can be set to active. The channel and group rows are checked for consistency, and an error in channels, architecture or configuration returns inconsistentValue. A channel cannot be added to a group that is already active.

An agent is not required to process an SNMP Set that touches several control objects in this MIB at once. This avoids conflicting varbinds in one PDU, such as activating a group while deactivating one of its channels.
sections.plainLanguage: First you list which roads belong in a team and number them in a row. Then you switch the team on, and the system checks that the list makes sense.

sections.title: Switch Commands and Group Settings
sections.content:
Protection switching is driven by ApsSwitchCommand values: clear, lockoutOfProtection, forcedSwitchWorkToProtect, forcedSwitchProtectToWork, manualSwitchWorkToProtect, manualSwitchProtectToWork and exercise. A command that cannot run because an equal or higher priority request is in effect returns inconsistentValue. noCmd is returned on reads when nothing has been written, and writing it returns wrongValue. For 1:n groups, ApsControlCommand adds lockoutWorkingChannel and clearLockoutWorkingChannel.

Group settings include revertive mode and direction. nonrevertive traffic stays on the protection line until another request arrives, and revertive traffic switches back once the fault clears. Revertive mode MUST be set for oneToN. Direction is unidirectional or bidirectional. Signal degrade and signal fail bit error rate thresholds and a wait-to-restore time are also configurable, and mode, revert and direction cannot change while the row is active.
sections.plainLanguage: An operator can press buttons such as switch now, stay put, or test the spare. Some buttons only work if nothing more important is already happening.

sections.title: K1/K2 Bytes, Status and Notifications
sections.content:
The ApsK1K2 textual convention stores the two-octet SONET APS protocol field. Bits 1 to 4 of K1 carry a request code such as 1111 Lockout of Protection, 1110 Forced Switch, 1000 Manual Switch, 0110 Wait-to-Restore and 0000 No Request. Bits 5 to 8 name the channel: 0 is the null channel, 1 to 14 are working channels and 15 is the extra traffic channel. K2 carries the channel, the architecture bit (0 for 1+1, 1 for 1:n) and the mode.

Status counters track events such as Channel Mismatch, Protection Switch Byte Failure (an inconsistent or invalid APS byte) and Far-End Protection-Line Failure. Per-channel counters cover signal degrades, signal failures and switchovers, with the time of the last switchover and the seconds service was carried on the protection line. Five notifications are defined: apsEventSwitchover, apsEventModeMismatch, apsEventChannelMismatch, apsEventPSBF and apsEventFEPLF. Each is sent when its counter increments, and apsNotificationEnable controls which are sent.
sections.plainLanguage: The equipment passes tiny coded messages saying what it wants. The MIB keeps score of what happened, such as how many times traffic moved to the spare, and can send an alert when it does.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Several writable objects can disrupt APS operation if set with malicious intent. The RFC names the command objects apsCommandSwitch and apsCommandControl, the group configuration objects such as apsConfigRowStatus, apsConfigMode and the thresholds, the channel configuration objects, and apsNotificationEnable.

SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security, and even a secure network gives no control over who on it can read or write these objects. The RFC recommends SNMPv3 with its cryptographic authentication and privacy, advises against deploying earlier versions, and leaves it to the operator to allow access only to legitimate principals.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone who could flip these switches could break the network, so only trusted people should get the remote control, and the connection should be locked.

items.label: noCmd
items.desc: Returned on reads; may not be written.

items.label: clear
items.desc: Clears the switch commands for the channel.

items.label: lockoutOfProtection
items.desc: Stops working channels switching to the protection line.

items.label: forcedSwitchWorkToProtect
items.desc: Forces a working channel onto the protection line.

items.label: forcedSwitchProtectToWork
items.desc: Forces traffic back to the working line.

items.label: manualSwitchWorkToProtect
items.desc: Manually moves a working channel to protection.

items.label: manualSwitchProtectToWork
items.desc: Manually moves traffic back to the working line.

items.label: exercise
items.desc: Tests the protocol for a switch of the channel.
